processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s before homogenization.
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 1000 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

processing_steps.method: isothermal constant strain rate compression (hot compression)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Strain rate = 1 s^-1 (this sample). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

structures.overall_structure: As-forged initial microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel (pre-deformation reference state): large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous etched boundaries, with dark grey grain interiors carrying abundant fine, closely spaced parallel light-grey striations/lamellae. The striation direction changes from grain to grain, giving a strongly banded, dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution, indicating chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition.

microstructure_list.region: as-forged billet / whole sample (before hot deformation)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: large polygonal grains spanning roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: isothermal constant strain rate compression; maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); heated to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s, homogenized 120 s, cooled at 5 °C/s, held 15 s, water-spray cooled after compression

characterization_methods.technique: Isothermal constant strain rate hot compression test
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1, maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92)
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the rheological (flow) stress behavior and hot deformation / dynamic recrystallization behavior of the steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The flow stress decreases as T increases and as ε̇ decreases; the steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material. Peak stress can be reduced by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etching solution 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; after sample preparation, grinding, polishing and etching
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure evolution and measure the DRX average grain size in the different deformation zones of the compressed sample.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure (Fig. 1) shows large polygonal grains with segregation banding; DRX degree ranks large deformation zone > small deformation zone > difficult deformation zone.

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius-type hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis with the Zener-Hollomon parameter and Cingara-McQueen critical-strain determination

analytical_models.equation_role: relates strain rate, peak stress and temperature to determine the dynamic recrystallization activation energy Q_p
analytical_models.model_note: ε̇ = A[sinh(ασp)]^n exp(-Q_p/RT); Q_p = 1000·R·k1·k2 = 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (average value over the experimental range).

analytical_models.equation_role: temperature-compensated strain rate used to normalize the flow-stress characteristic values
analytical_models.model_note: Z = ε̇ exp(Q_p/RT); lnZ values are tabulated in Table 1; for 1000 °C and 1 s^-1, lnZ = 63.29.

analytical_models.model_name: Cingara-McQueen equation (Eq 4) and DRX critical strain (Eq 9)
analytical_models.equation_role: determine the material constant C and the DRX critical strain εc

analytical_models.model_name: DRX characteristic value models vs lnZ (Eq 10)
analytical_models.equation_role: multiple linear regression fits relating the critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress of the flow stress curve to lnZ

computational_details.simulation_method: Finite element simulation with regression fitting (Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid plastic body, die indenter set as a rigid body; a semi-symmetric specimen used as the deformation model; contact friction set to the shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient of the billet and air set as 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation kept in line with the thermal compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and mean relative error MRE = 4.53% between predicted and experimental grain size; absolute error mostly within 3 µm.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: predict the DRX average grain size after hot deformation for numerical simulation
analytical_models.model_note: drex = 807743.63 ε̇^(-0.1903) exp(−120648.47/RT) + 4.338; initial grain size d0 and strain were taken as fixed values so a·d0^h·ε^p is treated as a constant. (Eq 11 general form: drex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT) + b.)

unmapped_findings: For the 1000 °C / 1 s^-1 condition, the Zener-Hollomon parameter value is lnZ = 63.29 (Table 1: row ε̇ = 1 s^-1, column T = 1000 °C).

The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, calculated from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine equation, is 669.844 kJ mol^-1; it is stated to be only the average value within the experimental range because the fitted lines in Fig. 4 are not parallel.

The material constant C from the Cingara-McQueen fit is 0.1461 (R = 0.9728), determined at 1050 °C and 0.01 s^-1 (not this sample's condition); the derived critical-to-peak strain relation is εc/εp ≈ 0.452.

The DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 it exceeds 70 µm, while at low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s^-1) the DRX grains are small but insufficient with remnant large original grains.

The recommended hot-working windows for a fine and uniform grain structure are 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C / 1–10 s^-1; the sample condition 1000 °C / 1 s^-1 does not fall within either of these stated windows.
The DRX grain-size prediction model (Eq 12) requires the initial grain size d0, but no numeric value for d0 is reported in the text.
